title: Enterprise On‑Prem Gated Signal Allocator for Isolated Networking
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Incoming customer requests for private/VPC/on‑prem deployments arrive via multiple channels (sales, support, solutions engineering, automated scanner). Signals are noisy and inconsistent: egress limits, bastion requirements, windowed maintenance, strict patching cycles, and legal controls vary across customers. We need a deterministic, auditable allocator that normalizes signals, applies risk/effort scoring, and assigns customers to a remediation lane with clear SLAs and next steps.

Goal: Build the "Gated Signal Allocator" (GSA) — a rules+score engine and lightweight UI surface that: 1) ingests signals from the intake pipeline, 2) normalizes predicates (networking posture, airgap constraints, upgrade cadence), 3) buckets requests into lanes (Self‑serve fastpass / Concierge / Engineering‑assisted / Decline with remediation), 4) surfaces required artifacts and owners, and 5) emits traceable decisions for audits and metrics.

Scope: MVP focuses on networking and upgrade constraints for on‑prem and air‑gapped requests. Not in scope: automated provisioning, license negotiations, or deep security assessments (those remain separate workflows).

Why now: Volume of private deploy requests with ambiguous network constraints is increasing; current manual triage causes >5 day median lead time and inconsistent outcomes. The GSA will reduce time to engagement, standardize comms, and create upstream signals for product roadmap and Dedicated capacity planning.
acceptance_criteria: GSA accepts normalized input from existing intake webhook and Support form (sample payload documented)
Rules engine outputs a lane assignment and a human‑readable rationale for every request (stored as a transcript)
Dashboard shows queue size by lane, median time to first contact, and % auto‑routed vs manual
Automated email templates rendered with required artifacts (network diagrams, maintenance windows) for each lane
Pilot with 5 customers (mix of airgapped and VPC) completes allocation and follow‑through within SLA windows (fastpass: 3 business days, concierge: 7 business days)
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose deterministic rule engine (simple DSL) over ML classifier for MVP to favor auditability and explainability — Aisha, Marco, Priya
2026-03-03: Bucketing schema finalized: fastpass / concierge / eng-assist / remediation-decline; kept 'eng-assist' narrow to limit engineering interrupts — Marco
2026-03-04: Opted to keep security assessment as a separate checkpoint; GSA will flag 'security-required' but not make the final security gating decision — Security (Lina)
next_steps: Draft intake normalization spec and sample payloads (owner: Marco) — due 2026-03-10
Prototype rule DSL and sample rules for common patterns (eg. egress-blocked + no bastion => concierge) — ENG spike (owner: Rafael) — 3d
Design small UI for ops to override lane assignments and capture rationale — DES sketch (owner: Mei) — draft due 2026-03-12
Run tabletop with Solutions Engineering and Support on 2026-03-17 to validate templates and SLAs
Create observability signals: allocation latency, override rate, downstream handoff failures — define dashboard widgets (owner: Observability team)
notes: We should avoid creating a hard 'decline' category without remediation guidance — instead the engine should always surface a remediation checklist and a templated comms path. Consider a future ML signal to surface ambiguous cases for human review. Keep the initial rules conservative to reduce false fastpass allocations.
